metadata.title: Power vs mass v2: animals, computing, spacecraft, and transportation

semantics.idle: Original v1 baseline meanings retained. New road: powered-on ready; air: ground idle; rockets: illustrative 70% of full fuel flow.
semantics.peak: Original v1 peak meanings retained. New road: estimated electrical peak; air: takeoff or maximum afterburner; rockets: modeled full-flow booster chemical input.
semantics.estimated: if true, connector is dashed because one or both endpoints are estimated/derived rather than directly published

metadata.inherited_data: All 32 v1 point records and their provenance retained verbatim; known v1 data-quality issues remain.
metadata.transport_power_basis: Battery-terminal electrical input for road vehicles; fuel mass flow times lower heating value (LHV) for aircraft and launch vehicles. Not shaft power or thrust times vehicle speed. Excludes upstream electricity/fuel production.
metadata.transport_mass_basis: RC includes batteries; scooter and car include a 75 kg rider/driver; aircraft use MTOW; rockets use full fueled reference stack mass. Fixed reference mass at both endpoints, not instantaneous mass during flight.
metadata.rocket_endpoint_caveat: Open marker is an illustrative powered state at 70% of full-flow chemical input, not idle, minimum throttle, or a claim about liftoff feasibility. Filled marker is modeled full booster flow at sea level. Upper-stage engines are not added to booster liftoff power.
metadata.source_scope: Source notes distinguish published inputs from assumptions. Derived values are engineering comparisons, not exact measurements of a complete operating vehicle.

reference_guide_semantics.mass_boundary: Cell mass only, excluding pack/stack auxiliaries, external reactant stores, and thermal-management hardware. Lines are not whole-system envelopes.
reference_guide_semantics.power_boundary: Peak electrical output, using reported power divided by cell mass or directly published specific power. No assumed energy-discharge duration conversion.
reference_guide_semantics.duration: Battery manufacturer specifies a 2 s pulse; SOFC reports a peak on measured V-I curves without a specified peak-hold duration.
reference_guide_semantics.sota_scope: Named contemporary high-performance benchmarks; not a universal world-record claim across all technologies and test conditions.
reference_guide_semantics.fuel_guides: Two dashed 5-minute (300 s) guides for ideal stoichiometric fuel-plus-carried-oxidizer mixtures: H2+O2 at 44.4 kW/kg and CH4+O2 at 33.3 kW/kg, from mixture specific energy divided by 300 s. These are chemical input per total propellant mass and exclude tanks, engines and hardware; they are not whole-system envelopes and use ideal ratios unlike fuel-rich rocket operation. See power_mass_peak_duration_survey.md.

mammal_bmr_scaling.note: General mammalian BMR scaling reference; some working idle values were derived/rounded.

mammal_mmr_scaling.note: Exercise-induced MMR scaling reference; equation reported as MMR_e = 16.7 M_b^0.87 with M_b in g and MMR in mL O2/h.

sled_dog_vo2max.note: Alaskan Husky VO2max ~198.7 mL/kg/min after training.

atlantic_salmon.note: Atlantic salmon MMR ~511 mg O2/kg/h; SMR work cross-checked against related literature.

atlantic_salmon_smr.note: Atlantic salmon SMR near ~168 mg O2/kg/h under one steady-flow condition.

dolphin_rest.note: Resting bottlenose dolphin metabolic rate ~2.15 W/kg.

killer_whale_bmr.note: Measured adult male killer-whale resting metabolism ~2275 W at mass 5318 kg.

killer_whale_behavior.note: Adult male killer-whale oxygen-consumption estimates up to 59.8 L O2/min across behaviors; used to derive representative high activity power.

blue_whale_fmr.note: Estimated blue-whale field metabolic rate 2679.1 MJ/day (~31 kW).

blue_whale_lunge.note: Lunge-feeding mechanics / energetics used as basis for ~0.6 MW transient upper-end working value.

iphone_2007.note: Apple states up to 250 h standby; working plot uses ~5.18 Wh battery / 250 h = 20.7 mW standby. Peak is an estimate.

macintosh_128k.note: Macintosh 128K: weight 16.5 lb, max watts 60 W.

ibm_pc_5150.note: Mass/power values are representative historical system values; current plot treats them as estimates.

cray_2.note: Working values: ~2494 kg and 150-200 kW; plot uses 200 kW peak.

eniac.note: Historical mass/power values are approximate; plot uses ~27.2 t and ~140 kW peak.

dgx_b300.note: 8x B300 GPUs. Busbar system mass 123 kg. Published power consumption 14.5 kW / max ~15 kW. Plot uses 19 kW as earlier working peak estimate; revise to 15 kW if strict-to-source.

gb300_nvl72.note: Fully loaded weight ~3300 lb (~1497 kg), 132 kW nominal TDP, ~155 kW electrical design peak.

frontier.note: Frontier system reference; plot uses ~24.6 MW peak and ~268.6 t estimated system mass from rack count × cabinet mass.

frontier_mass.note: Frontier cabinets ~8000 lb each; used with ~74 cabinets for mass estimate.

summit.note: Summit ~13 MW power footprint; mass estimate based on cabinet count × ~2500 lb/cabinet.

iss.note: ISS mass 419,725 kg; solar generation 75-90 kW. Plot baseline ~60 kW is estimated.

hubble.note: Hubble weight 12,200 kg; typical use ~2100 W; arrays >5200 W.

jwst.note: JWST total payload mass ~6200 kg. Plot uses ~2 kW available and ~1.2 kW baseline estimate.

voyager_1.note: Voyager 1 mass 721.9 kg; 3 RTGs at ~158 W each at launch (~474 W). Plot current ~225 W baseline is a recent-era working value.

starlink_v1.note: Starlink V1 mass 260 kg; solar-array-based estimate ~3540 W. Baseline 1500 W is estimated.

starlink_v2mini.note: V2 Mini mass ~800 kg; ~116 m^2 total surface area. Plot 10/28 kW values are engineering estimates.

starlink_v3.note: SpaceX says V3 arrays generate approximately 2x V2 power. Plot uses 2,000 kg and 22/56 kW working estimates.

marco.note: MarCO: 13.5 kg each; solar panels ~35 W near Earth, ~17 W near Mars. Baseline 10 W is estimated.

planet_dove.note: Dove mass is ~5 kg class; plot 5/15 W values are representative estimates and should be treated as such.

traxxas_xmaxx_mass.note: Manufacturer comparison dated 2021-07-06 lists X-Maxx mass 19.1 lb (about 8.66 kg). Plot assumes 10.1 kg with batteries; battery allowance is an estimate.

traxxas_xmaxx_8s.note: Manufacturer identifies 8S battery architecture and 30+ V. Plot uses 29.6 V nominal and assumes 100 A transient draw and 5 W ready power; neither input-power endpoint is a manufacturer measurement.

segway_max_g2_d.note: MAX G2 D: net mass 24.25 kg, nominal voltage 36 V, motor nominal/max rating 450/900 W, front light 2.1 W. Electrical peak is modeled separately as 36 V x assumed 30 A = 1080 W; vendor motor rating is not asserted to be battery-terminal power.

tesla_model3_mass.note: Model 3 Performance curb mass 4054 lb. Plot adds an assumed 75 kg driver. Published charging power is not used as propulsion power.

tesla_model3_power.note: Tesla official 2024-04-23 Model 3 Performance launch video description specifies 510 hp. Assumed 90% battery-to-shaft efficiency converts mechanical horsepower to electrical input. Ready draw 300 W is assumed, with HVAC off; variant is 2024 US Performance.

boeing_737_800_mass.note: Manufacturer lists 737-800 maximum takeoff mass 79010 kg and two CFM56-7B engines; the plot selects the CFM56-7B26 rating.

airbus_a380_mass.note: Manufacturer fact sheet gives 575 t maximum takeoff mass. The plot models four Trent 972-84 engines; configuration is representative, not a particular airline tail number.

icao_edb_2026.note: March 2026 workbook, sheet Gaseous Emissions and Smoke. Columns BZ and CC are takeoff and idle fuel flow in kg/s per engine. Selected rows below are not superseded in this release. Whole-aircraft power multiplies by engine count and assumed 43 MJ/kg LHV; APU omitted.

f16_mass.note: USAF lists maximum takeoff weight 37500 lb. Its paired 16875 kg value uses a rough conversion; the plot explicitly converts pounds with 0.45359237 kg/lb to 17009.7 kg. This is a family reference mass, not a verified tail-specific F100-PW-220 loading.

f16_f100_220_flow.note: Luke AFB caption states F-16 F100-220 maximum fuel flow 49964 lb/h. Plot converts that maximum to chemical input. Ground idle fuel flow 0.15 kg/s is an explicit engineering assumption, not a value stated by this source.

kerosene_lhv.note: NASA/TM-2006-214328 describes JP-8 LHV as about 43 MJ/kg. Plot applies 43 MJ/kg as a representative kerosene-class assumption for Jet A, JP-8, and RP-1, not a batch-specific certified value.

falcon9_overview.note: SpaceX lists whole-vehicle mass 549054 kg and first-stage sea-level thrust 7607 kN with nine Merlin engines. Plot uses that published mass as its fueled reference boundary, without adding a separate maximum payload.

rocket_model_reference.note: Research model uses Falcon 9 oxygen/RP-1 mass ratio 2.56. Plot adopts that ratio as a modeling assumption and assumes Merlin sea-level Isp 282 s; these are not new SpaceX-certified performance values.

starship_overview.note: SpaceX page snapshot lists upper-stage propellant 1600 t, booster propellant 3650 t, booster thrust 8240 metric ton-force, and 33 booster engines. Plot uses this stated configuration without claiming it describes every flight or future version. Adds assumed 550 t for combined dry hardware and payload to get a 5800 t fueled stack.

starship_mixture.note: 2022 FAA Starship/Super Heavy assessment, launch-vehicle description, gives 3.6:1 LOX/methane mass ratio. Reused as an explicit assumption for the modeled configuration; Isp 330 s is assumed. Current engine-specific mixture/flow can differ.

methane_lhv.note: Boeing Cascade energy model uses methane lower heating value 50 MJ/kg.

molicel_p60c_peak.note: Manufacturer claims 660 W peak for 2 seconds. This is a distinct pulse claim, not the 100 A discharge rating or a continuous-power guarantee. Pulse SOC/temperature/cutoff details are not given in the public feature statement.

molicel_p60c_mass.note: Tentative manufacturer datasheet v0.1 dated 2025-10-23: 75 g maximum cell mass.

sofc_metal_foam_2026.note: Ma et al., Advanced Science 2026, DOI 10.1002/advs.202517694: 6.56 kW/kg peak electrical specific power for metal-foam-supported SOFC at 650 C under humidified hydrogen. Laboratory cell boundary excludes stack interconnects, enclosure, insulation, balance of plant, fuel and oxidizer supply.

hydrogen_lhv.note: NASA/TM-2006-214328 gives hydrogen lower heating value about 120 MJ/kg. Combined with the ideal stoichiometric 8:1 oxygen-to-fuel mass ratio for 2 H2 + O2 -> 2 H2O, the H2+O2 mixture specific energy is about 13.33 MJ/kg of total propellant.

stoichiometric_fuel_oxygen_mixture.note: Ideal stoichiometric fuel-plus-carried-oxidizer mixture specific energy = fuel LHV / (1 + oxygen-to-fuel mass ratio), using rounded atomic masses. H2+O2: 120 MJ/kg / (1 + 8) = 13.33 MJ/kg. CH4+O2: 50 MJ/kg / (1 + 4) = 10.00 MJ/kg. Average chemical input per total mixture mass over a duration t is mixture specific energy / t. See power_mass_peak_duration_survey.md. These ideal ratios differ from the fuel-rich operating mixtures that inform the plotted rocket input power.

explosive_yields.note: Public yield and mass figures for illustrative off-scale explosive reference points. Little Boy (4,400 kg, 13-16 kt = 54-67 TJ) and Fat Man (4,670 kg, 18-23 kt = 75-96 TJ) from Wikipedia: Little Boy / Fat Man / Nuclear weapon yield. Tsar Bomba (27,000 kg, 50-58 Mt = 210-240 PJ) from Wikipedia: Tsar Bomba. MOAB (9,850 kg, 11 tons TNT = 46 GJ) from Wikipedia: GBU-43/B MOAB. Peak power is not a published specification; these use yield divided by an assumed energy-release time: about 1 microsecond for the nuclear prompt chain reaction (the Little Boy article states the chain reaction lasted less than 1 microsecond) and about 1 millisecond for the MOAB high-explosive detonation. Peak-power values are order-of-magnitude estimates, not measurements.

hawking_radiation.note: Hawking radiation power P = hbar * c^6 / (15360 * pi * G^2 * M^2). For M = 1 kg this gives about 3.56e32 W. Using the Planck-scale evaporation time t = 5120 * pi * G^2 * M^3 / (hbar * c^4) about 8.4e-17 s, so a 1 kg black hole releases its entire 9.0e16 J rest energy almost instantly. This is a theoretical (semiclassical) value.

figure_notes.s:
Transport: battery electrical input or fuel chemical input (LHV); aircraft masses at MTOW.
Road masses include batteries and rider/driver; rockets use fueled full-stack mass.
Rocket markers = full booster flow only; the modeled 70% flow state is hidden (data retained). Dashed = estimated / derived.
Original spacecraft retain electrical consumption / generation endpoints. See v2 notes for assumptions.
Battery/SOFC guides: peak electrical output per cell mass; exclude pack/stack auxiliaries.
Fuel guides: ideal stoichiometric H2+O2 / CH4+O2 chemical input per total propellant mass over 5 min.

reference_guides.label: Battery cell: 8.8 kW/kg (P60C, 2 s)
reference_guides.boundary: Manufacturer-claimed 2-second peak electrical output per cell mass; excludes pack hardware and cooling.

reference_guides.label: SOFC cell peak: 6.56 kW/kg (650°C)
reference_guides.boundary: Peak electrical output per laboratory cell mass at 650 C; excludes stack, fuel, oxidizer supply and balance of plant.

reference_guides.label: H2 + O2 stoich, 5 min: 44.4 kW/kg
reference_guides.boundary: Average chemical input per total stoichiometric H2+O2 mass burned over 5 minutes; excludes tanks, engines and hardware. Fuel-rich operating mixtures differ.

reference_guides.label: CH4 + O2 stoich, 5 min: 33.3 kW/kg
reference_guides.boundary: Average chemical input per total stoichiometric CH4+O2 mass burned over 5 minutes; excludes tanks, engines and hardware. Fuel-rich operating mixtures differ.

Little Boy / Fat Man
est. peak 6–9×10¹⁹ W
offscale_arrows.basis: Nuclear prompt chain reaction, yield over about 1 microsecond; both WW2 fission bombs shown as one off-scale arrow.

offscale_arrows.label:
MOAB
est. peak ~5×10¹³ W
offscale_arrows.basis: Conventional H-6 detonation, 46 GJ over about 1 millisecond; peak power is an order-of-magnitude estimate.

offscale_arrows.label:
Tsar Bomba
est. peak ~2×10²³ W
offscale_arrows.basis: Thermonuclear prompt chain reaction, 210 PJ over about 1 microsecond.

offscale_arrows.label:
1 kg black hole
Hawking power ~3.6×10³² W
offscale_arrows.basis: Hawking radiation P = hbar c^6 / (15360 pi G^2 M^2) at M = 1 kg; semiclassical theoretical value. Evaporates in ~8.4e-17 s.
